Marital status (single / married or cohabiting / divorced / widowed / other)
Number of children in household
Family responsibilities
Level of education (self) — from primary education to university level

Previous GPA / grades

Study goal (what do you want to achieve?)

Four factors: Teaching Presence (10 items, α = 0.92), Cognitive Presence (8 items, α = 0.91), Social Presence (9 items, α = 0.91), Emotional Presence (10 items, α = 0.93). Gender measurement invariance confirmed.

instruments.name: System Usability Scale
instruments.description: The most widely used questionnaire for assessing perceived usability of a system. Developed by Brooke (1996). Measures effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction. Industry average score is ~68 (not a percentage). Widely used for evaluating AI tutoring systems, eHealth apps, and digital learning tools.

list: 1. I think that I would like to use this system frequently.
2. I found the system unnecessarily complex. (REVERSE)
3. I thought the system was easy to use.
4. I think that I would need the support of a technical person to be able to use this system. (REVERSE)
5. I found the various functions in this system were well integrated.
6. I thought there was too much inconsistency in this system. (REVERSE)
7. I would imagine that most people would learn to use this system very quickly.
8. I found the system very cumbersome to use. (REVERSE)
9. I felt very confident using the system.
10. I needed to learn a lot of things before I could get going with this system. (REVERSE)

instruments.name: Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology
instruments.description: Unified model integrating eight technology acceptance theories (TRA, TAM, TPB, etc.). Developed by Venkatesh et al. (2003). Four core determinants of intention and use: Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, and Facilitating Conditions. Extended in UTAUT2 (2012) with Hedonic Motivation, Price Value, and Habit.

dataSources.label: Academic Records

dataSources.description: Objective metrics extracted from AI Tutor conversations to quantify learning orientation, scaffolding quality, and engagement patterns.

metrics.name: Conversational Engagement Score
metrics.description: Measuring turn counts and callbacks to distinguish dialogue from transactional queries

metrics.name: Learning Orientation Index
metrics.description: Detects exploratory learning (why/how questions) vs. answer-seeking

metrics.name: Scaffolding Resistance Score
metrics.description: Measures the extent to which students treat scaffolding as a barrier

metrics.name: Assignment Dependency Ratio
metrics.description: Detects when students use AI primarily to obtain solutions rather than engaging in exploratory learning

metrics.name: Bloom's Taxonomy Distribution
metrics.description: Categorizes and monitors cognitive level of student-AI interactions

collections.label: University Intake Battery
collections.description: Administered once when the student registers at the university. Independent of any specific course.

collections.label: Course Baseline Battery
collections.description: Administered at the registration of a specific course. Captures student-level and course-level pre-measures.

collections.label: AI Tutor Course Battery
collections.description: Administered for a specific course where the AI Tutor is used. Combines course-level measures with AI-specific perceptions.

collections.label: Post-Course Battery
collections.description: Administered at the end of a specific course. Captures outcomes, reflections, and post-course perceptions.

collections.label: AI Tutor Post-Course Battery
collections.description: Administered at the end of a specific course where the AI Tutor was used. Captures AI-specific acceptance, usability, and post-course perceptions.

collections.label: Study Success Prediction Battery
collections.description: Designed to predict study success across multiple courses. Combines baseline student characteristics with course-level engagement and outcome data.

protocols.label: Between-Cohorts
protocols.bestFor: Comparing with-AI vs. without-AI across semesters

protocols.label: Within-Course Crossover (AB-BA)
protocols.bestFor: Balancing order effects within a single course

protocols.label: Pre-During-Post (A/B/A)
protocols.description: Same course/cohort — switch conditions for all
protocols.bestFor: Examining transition effects within one cohort

researchQuestions.label: RQ1: Comparative Evaluation
researchQuestions.question: How does the interaction with the AI Tutor affect students' learning processes and outcomes, behavioral engagement, and psychological experience compared to a baseline (non-AI) condition?

researchQuestions.label: RQ2: Functional Evaluation
researchQuestions.question: How to assess the effectiveness of the AI Tutor functionalities with respect to its pedagogical design principles?
subQuestions: 2.1 Trust and attitude towards using AI Tutor
2.2 Learning behaviors with AI Tutor – guided scaffolding, personalization
